title: Deep Learning Experimentation
learning_outcomes: Explain building a small neural network and how it connects to deep learning experimentation.
Apply training and validation loops in the example and predict the output before running it.
Test one realistic edge case for deep learning experimentation and explain what the example does not prove.

content.intro: This lesson covers deep learning experimentation through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Connect neurons, layers, activations, losses, gradients, and training loops with small numerical examples. Large-scale training requires separate compute and engineering resources.

Confirm the idea with a small example and an explicit check rather than relying on fluent or plausible output.

items.title: Training and validation loops
items.text: For training and validation loops, distinguish the training objective from the evaluation goal. Check provenance and data quality, keep validation/test examples isolated from training, record the baseline and configuration, and evaluate both improvement on the target task and possible regressions elsewhere.

items.title: Plotting loss and metrics
items.text: Use plotting loss and metrics to turn a vague quality claim into an observable criterion. Define a representative dataset, an expected outcome or rubric, a baseline, and the failure categories you will record; interpret aggregate scores alongside examples and affected groups.

content_blocks.title: Provider and version note
content_blocks.text: Model names, API payloads, supported modalities, quotas, pricing, and SDK behavior vary by provider and change over time. Treat linked official documentation as the authority for a live integration; examples here avoid hard-coded production model IDs and secrets.

content.task: Practice building a small neural network within deep learning experimentation: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.
